Prior to playing in the [[NBA]], he played professionally for the YNG Dreamerz of the [[Overtime Elite]] League (OTE). ==High school career== Martin played high school basketball at [[Florida State University High School]] in [[Tallahassee, Florida]] under head coach and former NBA player [[Charlie Ward]]. ===Recruiting=== Coming out of high school, Martin was a highly ranked recruit in the class of 2022. He was ranked as a 4-star recruit by both [[ESPN]] and [[247Sports]] recruiting services.{{cite web |title=Jaylen Martin - ESPN recruiting |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/243392 |access-date=July 11, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}{{cite web|title=Jaylen Martin - 247Sports recruiting|url=https://247sports.com/player/jaylen-martin-46102426/|website=247Sports.com|access-date=July 11, 2023}} Despite receiving collegiate offers from [[University of Florida|Florida]], [[University of Georgia|Georgia]], [[Georgetown University|Georgetown]], [[Wake Forest University|Wake Forest]], [[University of Cincinnati|Cincinnati]], [[Texas Tech University|Texas Tech]] and [[University of Mississippi|Ole Miss]], he committed to play professionally in the [[Overtime Elite]] league.{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |date=September 3, 2021 |title=Overtime Elite (OTE) Signs Elite 2022 Wing Jaylen Martin |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/.amp/basketball/jaylen-martin-signs-with-overtime-elite |access-date=July 11, 2023 |website=SI.com |archive-date=July 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230711042748/https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/.amp/basketball/jaylen-martin-signs-with-overtime-elite |url-status=dead }} ==Professional career== ===YNG Dreamerz (2022–2023)=== Martin began his professional career playing for the YNG Dreamerz of the [[Overtime Elite]] league. He finished second in Overtime Elite's Most Improved Player voting and led the Dreamerz to the league Championship series, losing to the City Reapers. ===Westchester Knicks (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Martin signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New York Knicks]] on July 3, 2023,{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Sign Jaylen Martin to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-jaylen-martin-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2023|access-date=July 3, 2023}} but was waived on October 18.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Jaylen Martin and Isaiah Roby.|number=1714756011657957537|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}} On November 9, he was named to the opening night roster for the [[Westchester Knicks]]{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2023-24 Official Roster|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2023-24-official-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2023|access-date=November 28, 2023}} and on November 27, he signed another two-way contract with New York.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks sign Jaylen Martin to two-way contract|number=1729234923075309971|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=November 27, 2023|access-date=November 28, 2023}} However, he was waived on December 23 without playing for New York{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Jaylen Martin|number=1738573984071852327|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=December 23, 2023|access-date=January 1, 2024}} and returned to Westchester three days later.{{cite tweet|author=Westchester Knicks|title=Jaylen Martin returns to the Westchester Knicks as a returning rights player.|number=1739744745897734642|user=wcknicks|date=December 26, 2023|access-date=January 1, 2024}} ===Brooklyn / Long Island Nets (2024–2025)=== On February 21, 2024, Martin signed a two-way contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]],{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Jaylen Martin to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-jaylen-martin-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2024|access-date=February 22, 2024}} but was waived on January 1, 2025.{{cite web |date=January 1, 2025 |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Tosan Evbuomwan to Two-way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-tosan-evbuomwan-to-two-way-contract |access-date=January 1, 2025 |website=NBA.com}} ===Delaware Blue Coats (2025)=== On January 11, 2025, Martin joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] after his rights were traded from the [[Westchester Knicks]] in exchange for the returning player rights of [[David Duke Jr.]] and a 2025 future first-round pick.{{cite tweet|author=Delaware Blue Coats|title=OFFICIAL: the Delaware Blue Coats acquire
